report.source_text: Histological examination of a skin biopsy from a violaceous nodule on his left palm revealed a malignant vascular proliferation and spindle cells that were positive for HHV8 by immunohistochemistry, consistent with KS (figure 1). Concurrently, a biopsy of a scaly erythematous skin lesion on his right arm (figure 2) revealed an atypical infiltrate of predominantly CD4-positive T-cells with mild epidermotropism and partial loss of CD7 expression assessed by immunohistochemistry (figure 3). Molecular studies performed on the latter biopsy showed clonal TCR gene rearrangement, indicating the presence of a T-cell clonal population, most consistent with CTCL.

report.source_text: Serologies were negative for viral hepatitis, syphilis, HIV, and human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV)-I/II and were positive for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). PCR testing on the peripheral blood was positive for HHV8 (non-quantitative) and EBV (4786 copies /mL), while PCR for HIV and cytomegalovirus (CMV) was negative (below the detection level).

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 88-year-old Inuit man presented with violaceous subcutaneous nodules and erythematous, scaly skin lesions, along with systemic symptoms. Skin biopsies confirmed two synchronous conditions: Kaposi Sarcoma (HHV8 positive) from a violaceous nodule and Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma (consistent with Mycosis Fungoides, with atypical CD4+ T-cells, CD7 loss, and clonal TCR gene rearrangement) from a scaly lesion. HIV serology was negative, confirming HIV-negative Kaposi Sarcoma.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with violaceous subcutaneous nodules on palms and lower extremities and rapid onset total body erythematous, pruritic and scaly skin lesions.

Histological examination of a skin biopsy from a violaceous nodule revealed a malignant vascular proliferation and spindle cells positive for HHV8 by immunohistochemistry, consistent with Kaposi Sarcoma (KS).

A biopsy of a scaly erythematous skin lesion revealed an atypical infiltrate of predominantly CD4-positive T-cells with mild epidermotropism and partial loss of CD7 expression, and molecular studies showed clonal TCR gene rearrangement, indicating a T-cell clonal population most consistent with Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma (CTCL), consistent with the Mycosis Fungoides (MF) subtype.
Both conditions were diagnosed concurrently from biopsies taken on admission, indicating synchronous occurrence.
HIV serology was negative, confirming HIV-negative Kaposi Sarcoma.
